formally recognised by councils
around Australia, so crags stay open and get the good stuff: stairs, signs and proper tracks. In Queensland we work under ACAQ.

title: About
heading: Climbers, for the long *haul*
lede: Acacia Climbing Coalition is a small, volunteer-run crew working to get outdoor climbing recognised and looked after across Australia. We're starting in South East Queensland, and building it in the open.
seoDescription: Who we are, why we started, and how we work with councils to get outdoor climbing recognised across Australia.

sections.heading: Why we started

children.text: Most councils in Australia don't have a way to formally recognise outdoor climbing. That leaves crags with unclear access, no stairs or signs, and nobody speaking for climbers when decisions get made.
At the same time, more people than ever are climbing in gyms and wanting to head outside, with very little to tell them where it's okay to go and how to look after it when they get there.

sections.quoteBody: A crag that's mapped, written up and known to council is a lot easier to keep open. So that's what we do, one crag at a time, and we share every step along the way.

sections.label: Every crag goes through the same eight steps
sections.heading: How we do it
steps: Research the area, its history and its climbing
Reach out to guidebook authors and locals
Talk with council and park rangers
Site visits: GPS, photos and mapping on KAYA

cards.title: Tooheys Forest recognised
cards.body: Brisbane City Council formally recognises bouldering at Tooheys, with new stairs and signage now in.

cards.title: White Rock and Plunketts
cards.body: Talking with Ipswich and Logan councils about formal access, with site visits and mapping underway.

cards.title: Digital guidebooks
cards.body: Documenting our crags on KAYA, so every crag is properly on the record.

cards.title: More of Australia
cards.body: Cedar Creek and Passchendaele are just getting started. After SEQ, the plan is every state.

cards.title: Who's behind it
cards.body: Right now Acacia is a small volunteer crew, coordinated by Cooper, who is also the bouldering representative for ACAQ, Queensland's peak climbing access body. Everything here gets done in spare hours, with a lot of help from local climbers.

items.title: ACAQ
items.body: Queensland's peak climbing access body. Our Queensland work happens under their umbrella.

items.title: KAYA
items.body: Where our digital guidebooks live, so climbers have accurate, up-to-date info.

items.title: Local councils
items.body: Brisbane, Ipswich, Logan, Moreton Bay and Southern Downs, so far.

children.text: The crags we document sit on the lands of many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, including the Turrbal, Jagera, Yugarapul, Jinibara and Kabi Kabi peoples in South East Queensland. We pay our respects to Elders past and present.
We want consultation with Traditional Owners to be part of how every crag is documented, not an afterthought. We're still building those relationships, and we'll share how that's going as it happens.

title: Get involved
heading: Every bit *helps*
lede: We're a small crew, so a bit of help goes a long way. Pick whatever suits you, flick us an email, and we'll take it from there.
seoDescription: Volunteer, report a crag issue, help with council letters or chip in. Every bit helps keep Australian crags open.

cards.title: Give an hour or two
cards.body: Crag clean-ups, track work, site visits and mapping. Weekends mostly, and no experience needed beyond knowing your way around a crag.

cards.title: Be our eyes on the ground
cards.body: Closed tracks, new signs, damage, a gate that wasn't there last week. Tell us what you've seen, where and when, and we'll log it and follow it up.

cards.title: Help with council letters
cards.body: When a council is deciding something, letters from local climbers really count. We'll let you know when it matters and help with what to say.

cards.title: Chip in for the crags
cards.body: Donations go straight to signage, mapping and council submissions. We're not a registered charity yet, so it isn't tax-deductible for now.

sections.label: Not in South East Queensland?
sections.heading: We want to hear from climbers everywhere
sections.body: We're starting in SEQ, but the goal is every state. If there's a crag near you with access worries, or you're already looking after one, tell us about it. It all helps shape where we go next.

children.text: This site is run by Acacia Climbing Pty Ltd (ABN 38 237 542 815), trading as Acacia Climbing Coalition, based in Queensland, Australia.
We don't have accounts, forms or newsletters on this site. If you email us, we receive your name, email address and whatever you choose to tell us.
Our host, Cloudflare, keeps basic technical logs (like IP addresses) to keep the site running and secure.
We only use what you send us to reply to you, coordinate volunteering, and follow up crag reports. We don't sell or share your details, and we'll delete them if you ask.
We handle personal information in line with the Australian Privacy Principles. Email hello@acaciaclimbing.org with any questions or requests.
Access status and crag details here are general information, not permission to climb. Access can change, so always check signage, local rules and any closures before you visit.
Climbing is risky. You're responsible for your own safety and for respecting the land, other users and Traditional Owners.
You're welcome to share and link to anything here with credit to Acacia Climbing Coalition. Detailed guidebook information lives on KAYA under their terms.
